title: Making Droplet-Embedded Vesicles to Model Cellular Lipid Droplets
protocol: Wash the two ITO coated glass plates with water.
Dry the two ITO coated glass plates and wash them with ethanol.
Wear gloves and work under a laminar flow hood when using chloroform.
Wash the two ITO coated glass plates with chloroform.
Dilute a DOPC 99.5% (w/w) and Rh-DOPE 0.5% (w/w) mixture in 200 μL of chloroform at 2 mg/mL for DOPC.
Homogenize the phospholipid mixture by vortexing.
Collect 20 μL with a microsyringe and make little droplet spots (2 μL) on the ITO coated glass inside the PDMS chamber.
Desiccate the lipid film during 1 hour in a vacuum chamber.
Clip the electroformation chamber with fold back clips.
Add very slowly 3 mL of sucrose solution into the chamber.
Apply 100 Hz AC voltage at 1.4 Vpp using conductive alligator clip between the generator and the aluminum strips.
Maintain the voltage for at least 2 hours.
Collect GUVs gently with a Pasteur pipette in two Eppendorf tubes of 1.5 mL.
Store the collected GUVs at 4°C.
Prepare two empty Eppendorf tubes of 0.5 mL cleaned with an air stream for the production of DEVs.
Add 70 μL of HKM buffer to the first Eppendorf tube.
Filter the HKM buffer using a 0.45μm filter to ensure it is clean and dust-free.
Check for large particles in the filtered buffer by placing a small volume on a Menzel coverslip and observing under a microscope.
Vortex the Eppendorf tube containing the oil and HKM buffer to form a coarse emulsion.
Sonicate the solution until it becomes cloudy, indicating formation of a nano-emulsion.
Homogenize the solution by vortexing after sonication.
Add 5 μL of triolein oil into the HKM volume and close the Eppendorf tube.
Prepare a 200 μl micropipette and cut the cone of the pipette 5 mm from the tip to obtain a truncated cone with a large aperture.
Vortex the first Eppendorf tube containing triolein for 10 s to create a coarse emulsion.
Sonicate the emulsion with the water bath sonicator for 10 seconds until the solution starts to become cloudy.
Vortex the mixture again for 10 seconds.
Sonicate the mixture again for 10 seconds to obtain a nano-emulsion.
Collect rapidly 50 μL of the nano-emulsion using the truncated cone pipette tip.
Pour this volume very gently into an Eppendorf tube containing the GUVs solution.
Mix back and forth very gently with the same truncated pipette tip to homogenize the GUVs and nano-droplets mixture.
Place the Eppendorf tube on a rotating tube mixer for 5 minutes.
Take a Menzel glass coverslip for confocal microscopy observation.
Pipette 80 μl of BSA solution onto the coverslip and wait for 10 seconds.
Place the BSA solution on the glass coverslip.
Discard the BSA solution after 10 seconds.
Rinse the BSA-treated spot with HKM buffer three times.
Deposit an 80 μL HKM solution onto the washed coverslip.
Add a 20 μL DEV solution to the HKM solution on the coverslip.
Place the coverslip under the microscope for observation.
Remove the BSA solution with a pipette.
Rinse the BSA spot on the coverslip with 80 μL of HKM buffer and discard this solution.
Repeat this process three times.
Deposit 80 μL of HKM buffer on the glass coverslip, on the BSA-treated spot.
Place the coverslip on the microscope for observation.
Prepare a 20 μL micropipette to collect 10 μL of the DEV solution with pipette tip cut 5 mm from the tip.
Collect gently 10 μL of the DEVs solution with the micropipette.
Pour the collected DEV solution into the HKM solution on the glass coverslip.
Wait 5 min for the DEVs to settle down on the coverslip.
Cleared excess non-GUV-incorporated nano-droplets from the observation regions of the DEVs.
